posts.text: This week: a ceasefire that didn't hold, a leadership reshuffle, a border that opened after 118 years, a typhoon, and an earthquake that's now a political crisis. Five stories, five moving lines on the map — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ US strikes hit Iran again; Tehran retaliated by hitting American bases in Bahrain, Kuwait & Jordan. Iran fired on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz — 33km wide, ~1/5 of world oil. Brent crude jumped 4%+. (Al Jazeera, Guardian, NYT, DW)

2/ Zelensky reshuffled Ukraine's government, replacing PM Svyrydenko, as Macron hosted Kyiv+Paris+London+Berlin talks. Poland, meanwhile, is weighing cutting Ukraine's arms aid over a WWII-era border dispute. (BBC, DW, NYT, Guardian)

3/ Gibraltar and Spain just opened their border after 118 years of checkpoints — a line dating to the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht. Sovereignty unchanged, but free movement returns to one of Europe's oldest disputed frontiers. (BBC)
4/ Typhoon Bavi — at peak roughly the width of France — made landfall in eastern China. ~2 million evacuated in Zhejiang alone, after the storm killed 17 in the Philippines. (BBC, NYT)

5/ Venezuela's earthquake death toll passed 4,300, nearly 3 weeks on. Now it's political: residents of a flattened government housing project are furious at Chávez's heirs over the slow response. (Guardian, NYT)

The historical parallel: Poland's borders, overlaid across 1000, 1596, 1939 & 1945. The 1939 line reached deep into today's western Ukraine — including Volhynia, where WWII's disputed killings happened. 1945 shoved Poland ~200km west. Full issue ⬇️
